sections.html:
The McDowell County registrar is at 35 West Fort Street in Marion. Call 828-652-4727. Weekday hours are 8:30am to 5:00pm. Online services live at McDowellDeeds.com.

Staff record, index and store real estate and business paper. Marriage licenses, notary oaths, military discharge records and certified birth and death copies come through the same door. For a seller, the land side is what counts: the goal is a public record that is complete, accurate and safe.

sections.h2: Can a McDowell County deed be filed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. All document types qualify, and three vendors are named, which lets an attorney in another city file without driving to Marion.

E-recording vendors for McDowell County
VendorTelephone
Simplifile1-800-460-5657
Electronic Document Logistics (EDL)1-919-341-4101
Corporation Service Company (CSC)1-866-652-0111

The choice of vendor belongs to your attorney or title company. You only need the signed deed ready.

G.S. 161-10 governs, and the county adds nothing of its own. Typical line items:

  • Ordinary deed: a $26.00 base for the first 15 pages, plus $4.00 per added page.
  • Mortgage or deed of trust: a $64.00 base for 35 pages, plus $4.00 per added page.
  • Lender's release: free.
  • Plat: $21.00 a sheet.
  • Certified copy: $5.00 for the first page, $2.00 for the rest.
  • Nonstandard format: $25.00 extra. A second instrument inside one document: $10.00 extra.

Payment is due before filing. If you are sending a 60-page bundle of exhibits, phone 828-652-4727 and have the office total the charge first.

Sellers carry this tax in McDowell County. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the rate is one dollar for each $500 of price, and a leftover amount under $500 is rounded up. The registrar will not record until it is paid.

The county's general fund keeps one share. The state gets the other share each month, minus refunds and the county's allowance.

Find the figure in the seller column of the closing statement, below the loan payoff line.

sections.h2: Parcel maps and the assessor after recording
sections.html:
GIS mapping in the assessor's office processes deed transfers and updates the maps, and it also serves as plat review officer. Deed transfers and parcel maps are handled by the same people, so check the map once your deed is recorded.

Find the assessor at 60 E. Court Street on the same weekday schedule. Real property, mapping and land records each have their own extension. A 2027 real property reappraisal is coming, and the new values will fall on whoever owns the house then.

  • Ask mapping whether your parcel shows the shape and acreage you expect.
  • Ask real property staff what the reappraisal could do to your assessment.
  • A link on the assessor's page lets you report storm damage.

Tax Collections is in the same County Services Building and keeps the same 8:30am to 5:00pm hours. Email taxcollections@mcdowellnc.gov or call (828) 652-0701 for a payoff on the current bill. With both offices under one roof, you can settle the value question and the payoff question in a single trip.

sections.h2: Property tax relief that affects a buyer
sections.html:
Find out early if your parcel sits in a relief program, because several end or come due when the house transfers. Applications go to 60 East Court Street between January 1 and May 31, with all paperwork back by June 1. No one may combine programs.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the home and one acre lose the greater of $25,000 or half of their assessed value. No lien is created. The owner must be 65 by January 1 or totally disabled. Phone the office for the yearly income cap.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 comes off the assessed value after one application. Age and income do not matter.
  • Circuit breaker: you must have owned and lived in the home five years and reapply each June 1. Three years of deferred tax sit as a lien that comes due on a death, a transfer or a move.
  • Present-use value: for farm, forest or horticultural land, requested in January. Forest land needs a sound management plan.

If the parcel is in present-use value or carries deferred circuit breaker tax, tell your closing attorney so the back amounts are counted in the settlement.

When the county sues over unpaid tax under G.S. 105-374, the sale itself happens at the courthouse, 21 S. Main St. in Marion. Whoever bids highest must give the commissioner $1,000.00 in cash right away.

Ten days follow for upset bids, filed with the clerk. Any new bid must exceed the last by 5 percent, and by at least $750.00. Each raised bid restarts the ten-day clock. The clerk's number is (828) 655-4100.

  • Upcoming sales are posted through the county's foreclosure page.
  • Look up map, assessed value, acreage and deed reference in the GIS by parcel number.
  • Wells and septic are left for the bidder to research.

An owner who has fallen behind can skip the auction by selling first. Ask the tax collector for a payoff number while no sale date is set.

Priority goes to whoever registers first. G.S. 47-18 says a deed does nothing against lien creditors or paying purchasers until it is filed where the land sits, and for McDowell land that means Marion.

For that reason attorneys file the deed and the buyer's loan papers as a set. They also pursue stale releases, which cost only the time a lender takes to respond. When the title search shows a lien that was never cancelled, ask the attorney to request the release at once.

sections.h2: What to bring to a McDowell County closing
sections.html:
Your attorney does the filing, but a few items on your side save days.

  • Your vesting deed, so the legal description and owner names can be copied exactly.
  • Payoff letters for every loan secured by the house, with a note on which lender will file the release.
  • The parcel number from your tax bill, for checking the GIS map after recording.
  • The assessor's reply on any relief program or deferred circuit breaker tax.
  • For an inherited house, estate papers that show who has authority to sign.

Once the deed is filed, confirm the new owner's name with the assessor and the collector, so the following bill reaches the right person. A call to the registrar at 828-652-4727 confirms the filing date and gives you the reference you need for your records.

The mid-2025 population was 45,198, compared with 44,578 in 2020, living in 22,036 housing units. Roughly 75.6 percent of homes have owners living in them, and the middle owner-occupied house was valued at $171,100 for 2020 to 2024. Builders pulled 164 permits in 2025.

Inherited houses, probate sales and homes that need work often lead owners to ask for cash offers. That kind of buyer can close the day the deed is ready to file.

Whichever route you choose, a clean record makes the closing quick. Pull your deed from McDowellDeeds.com, confirm every old loan has a recorded release, and ask mapping to verify the parcel before a buyer's surveyor does.

faqs.q: What days is the McDowell County registrar open?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm, at 35 West Fort Street. The number is 828-652-4727.

faqs.q: Which vendors file McDowell County deeds electronically?
faqs.a: Simplifile, EDL (Electronic Document Logistics) and CSC (Corporation Service Company). The county accepts any document this way.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to file a 12-page deed in McDowell County?
faqs.a: $26.00, because the base fee reaches 15 pages. Deeds of trust have a $64.00 base through page 35.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay the deed tax in McDowell County?
faqs.a: The seller, at $1.00 per $500 of price, paid at the counter before filing.

faqs.q: What is the minimum upset bid at a McDowell County tax sale?
faqs.a: Five percent over the last bid, with a floor of $750.00 more. The clerk's office takes it, and the ten-day clock starts over.
